catalog_quote: §2.5.5: In many cases, several phonological processes occur with the addition of a suffix in keeping with phonotactic constraints. Rigid stress and syllable rules govern vowels in Kumzari words. When a suffix is added, penultimate syllable stress is maintained through vowel changes, insertions, and deletions. All three processes occur in the following word: raising and fronting of the a to ē, deletion of the i, and insertion of an epenthetic u: tarqit ‘wedding poem’ tēruqt-ō ‘the wedding poem’. In a process of resyllabification, when labial-initial verb roots are prefixed with the imperfect t-, the verb root vowel becomes an epenthetic vowel inserted after the prefix, stress shifts to the prefix, and the verb root vowel is rounded to u: ... bēr ‘carry’ tē-bur ... In an open syllable, a final short a may inherit stress and be lengthened when a suffix is added to the word: kahraba ‘electr…
sweep_summary: One sweep item only (Anonby 2013, Orientalia Suecana LXI: 54-58), already listed in the per-language bibliography and already held on file from the 2026-09-16 audit (DiVA host still refuses connections; held copy is the Wayback capture; Read in full: it is a first-hand, stress-specific study and states explicitly (p. 57) that Kumzari stress is by default penultimate, that word-final monosyllabic suffixes are never stressed, and that -an PL and -ō DEF shift stress to the new penult (with stem-vowel lengthening/harmonization) whereas the existential clitic =in and INDEF -ē are stress-neutral, yielding surface antepenultimate stress ('birmitin, 'birmitē). This confirms the catalog's penultimate default and refines its 'rigid, maintained under suffixation' prule toward a morphologically conditioned (stem-based) stress domain, matching the recode recommendation already filed in Anonby 2011:378 and Anonby 2012/13:56-58, set dom=true). The catalog's deciding source (van der Wal Anonby 2015 grammar, §2.5.5) stays the fuller reference description, but the Anonby 2013 p. 57 statement is the better explicit statement of the stress rule. Nothing left unread; no acquisition priorities.

new_statements.quote: In Kumzari, however (similar to a common pattern in Arabic), stress is by default placed on a word's penultimate syllable: 'birmit 'hard candy', 'gambil 'hole'. Word-final monosyllabic suffixes, then, are never stressed in Kumzari. However, in some cases they cause word stress to shift toward the end of a word: while the simple plural suffix -an, introduced above, causes stress to shift to the second-last syllable of the resulting word, the existential plural clitic -in does not.

new_statements.reading: Penultimate default stress on the word, but with morphological conditioning: cohering suffixes (-an PL, -ō DEF) are inside the stress domain and pull stress to the new penult (with stem-vowel lengthening/harmonization), while stress-neutral suffixes/clitics (-ē INDEF, =in existential) sit outside it, giving surface antepenultimate stress ('birmitē, 'birmitin). Corroborated by the same author's JIPA Illustration (Anonby 2011: 378, held): 'On morphologically simple words of more than one syllable, stress falls predictably on the penultimate syllable... stress placement is contrastive for morphologically complex words.' Catalog's fixed-penultimate coding is confirmed for the default; its prule wording ('rigid... penultimate syllable stress is maintained' under suffixation) is refined: stress domain is stem-based / morphologically conditioned (dom=true), not rigid across all suffixation.

audit.recode_to: Keep fixed penultimate as the default (monomorphemic words and stem+cohering suffix -ō DEF, -an PL), but set morphological conditioning (dom=true / stem-based stress domain) and rewrite prule: stress-neutral suffix -ē INDEF and existential enclitics =in etc. do not move stress, giving surface antepenultimate stress (ˈbirmitē 'a hard candy', ˈqēčūbē 'a walking stick', ˈbirmitin); possessed-plural -ā takes final stress (rōrā´ yē). Drop the word 'rigid... maintained under suffixation' generalisation; add Anonby 2011:378 and Anonby 2012/2013:56-58 to sources.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding §2.5.5 quotation and both supporting loci are verbatim in the held Leiden chapter PDFs at the stated pages. (2) The deciding source is the 2015 reference grammar (best overall description, open access, held in full), but its stress claim is a one-sentence remark inside a morphophonology subsection; the grammar has no stress section. The two stress-specific publications listed in Glottolog (Anonby 2011 JIPA Illustration; Anonby 2012/13 Orientalia Suecana), fetched sources and read now, agree that default stress is penultimate but state explicitly that 'stress placement is contrastive for morphologically complex words': indefinite -ē and the existential enclitics are stress-neutral (ˈbirmitē, ˈqēčūbē = antepenultimate surface stress), whereas -ō and -an shift stress to the new penult with lengthening/harmonization. This directly contradicts the record's prule wording
audit.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE CHECK (re-done independently): the deciding §2.5.5 quotation is verbatim in the held Ch.2 text lines 942-972, spanning the printed page break '40 A Grammar of Kumzari' (= pp.39-40): 'Rigid stress and syllable rules govern vowels in Kumzari words. / When a suffix is added, penultimate syllable stress is maintained through vowel changes, insertions, and deletions.' with tarqit > tēruqt-ō, tē-bur, kahrabā-ō exactly as cited. Supporting loci also verified: Ch.1 ( l.998-999) 'Kumzari has developed penultimate-syllable stress'; Ch.3 ( l.1710-1717)
